newsitem.title: UK: UK plans powerful new competition authority - FT.
newsitem.headline: UK plans powerful new competition authority - FT.

text.p: Britain is to replace its Monopolies and Mergers Commission (MMC) with a new competition authority with wider powers, the Financial Times reported on Friday.

The Competition Commission will assume the functions of the MMC and also hear appeals against the decisions of the director general of fair trading under new measures to be introduced next year, the report said.
It said the plans, the work of Trade and Industry Secretary Margaret Beckett, would be contained in a consultation paper to be issued in the next two weeks together with a draft bill.

The bill will introduce a ban on anti-competitive agreements such as price-fixing or market-sharing cartels and anti-competitive behaviour, such as predatory pricing, by companies which dominate their markets.
Companies breaking the law will risk fines of up to 10 percent of their worldwide turnover, the report said.
They would be imposed by the director general of fair trading, with a right to appeal against his decisions to the Competition Commission.
